import statistics

# Treasury liability data (in millions of dollars)
# June 1991
europe_1991 = 268166
latam_1991 = 337565

# June 1996
europe_1996 = 426245
latam_1996 = 443872

print("=== Step 1: Treasury Liability Data ===")
print(f"June 1991 - Europe: {europe_1991} millions")
print(f"June 1991 - Latin America & Caribbean: {latam_1991} millions")
print(f"June 1996 - Europe: {europe_1996} millions")
print(f"June 1996 - Latin America & Caribbean: {latam_1996} millions")

# Step 2: Linear regression with Europe as predictor of Latin America
# We have two data points: (Europe_1991, LatAm_1991) and (Europe_1996, LatAm_1996)
x = [europe_1991, europe_1996]
y = [latam_1991, latam_1996]

# Calculate OLS: slope = sum((x-xbar)(y-ybar)) / sum((x-xbar)^2)
xbar = statistics.mean(x)
ybar = statistics.mean(y)
print(f"\n=== Step 2: Linear Regression ===")
print(f"xbar (Europe mean): {xbar}")
print(f"ybar (LatAm mean): {ybar}")

numerator = sum((xi - xbar) * (yi - ybar) for xi, yi in zip(x, y))
denominator = sum((xi - xbar) ** 2 for xi in x)
slope = numerator / denominator
intercept = ybar - slope * xbar

print(f"Slope: {slope}")
print(f"Intercept: {intercept}")
print(f"Regression: LatAm = {slope} * Europe + {intercept}")

# Step 3: Germany's GDP growth
# GDP in billions
gdp_1991 = 1875.79  # billion USD
gdp_1996 = 2506.58  # billion USD

gdp_growth_rate = (gdp_1996 - gdp_1991) / gdp_1991 * 100
print(f"\n=== Step 3: Germany's GDP ===")
print(f"1991 GDP: {gdp_1991} billion")
print(f"1996 GDP: {gdp_1996} billion")
print(f"GDP growth rate: {gdp_growth_rate:.4f}%")

# Step 4: Counterfactual
# Apply Germany's GDP growth rate to June 1991 Europe value
europe_counterfactual = europe_1991 * (1 + gdp_growth_rate/100)
print(f"\n=== Step 4: Counterfactual ===")
print(f"June 1991 Europe: {europe_1991}")
print(f"Counterfactual Europe (applying GDP growth): {europe_counterfactual}")

# Use regression to predict corresponding Latin America value
latam_predicted = slope * europe_counterfactual + intercept
print(f"Predicted Latin America (from regression): {latam_predicted}")

# Step 5: Absolute difference from actual
abs_diff = abs(latam_predicted - latam_1996)
print(f"\n=== Step 5: Difference Calculation ===")
print(f"Actual June 1996 Latin America: {latam_1996}")
print(f"Predicted Latin America: {latam_predicted}")
print(f"Absolute difference: {abs_diff}")

# Express as percentage of actual June 1996 value
pct_of_actual = (abs_diff / latam_1996) * 100
print(f"Absolute difference as % of actual: {pct_of_actual:.4f}%")

# Step 6: US total liabilities growth (Europe + Latin America as proxy)
us_liabilities_1991 = europe_1991 + latam_1991
us_liabilities_1996 = europe_1996 + latam_1996
us_liabilities_growth = (us_liabilities_1996 - us_liabilities_1991) / us_liabilities_1991 * 100
print(f"\n=== Step 6: US Liabilities Growth ===")
print(f"US Liabilities 1991 (Europe + LatAm): {us_liabilities_1991}")
print(f"US Liabilities 1996 (Europe + LatAm): {us_liabilities_1996}")
print(f"US Liabilities growth rate: {us_liabilities_growth:.4f}%")

# Final calculation
# Multiply percentage by ratio of US growth to Germany GDP growth
ratio = us_liabilities_growth / gdp_growth_rate
print(f"\nRatio (US growth / Germany GDP growth): {ratio:.4f}")

final_result = pct_of_actual * ratio
print(f"\n=== FINAL RESULT ===")
print(f"Final value (rounded to 2 decimal places): {final_result:.2f}")
